previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, recurrent cellulitis, and chronic pancreatitis was admitted for persistent nausea and vomiting with inability to tolerate oral intake. Initial evaluation showed stable vital signs, normal labs including lipase and liver function tests, and a normal CT head. She was treated with IV fluids and prochlorperazine for symptom control. Her home OxyContin dose was reduced due to concern for narcotic-induced nausea, and she was started on Cymbalta for neuropathic pain. Her platelet count dropped to a nadir of 73 but recovered to 91 by discharge, likely due to recent antibiotics. She reported guaiac-positive stool on discharge morning, attributed to known hemorrhoids, requiring GI follow-up. She improved clinically, advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged home on revised medications including reduced OxyContin, continued Keflex suppression, and new prochlorperazine and duloxetine.

#Neuro:
Ms. ___ initially presented to the ___ Emergency 
Department on ___ following a transient episode of 
word-finding difficulty. In the ED, her language exam showed 
intact repetition, fluency, comprehension, and naming. NCHCT was 
neg for acute intracranial hemorrhage. CTA was attempted but 
could not be completed due to IV infiltration. MRI was neg for 
acute stroke (please note, patient has an MRI-compatible PPM and 
was cleared by electrophysiology). Her admission labs showed 
sub-therapeutic INR of 1.5 (goal INR ___ per records). Given 
imaging findings neg for stroke and resolution of her symptoms 
back to baseline, her presentation was initially thought to be 
consistent with a TIA in the setting of sub-therapeutic INR. She 
presented with a second episode of confusion and word-finding 
difficulty at 4 am on ___ during this admission after waking 
up to go to the bathroom. At that time, her INR was therapeutic 
at 2.1. Given therapeutic INR during this episode and rapid 
return to her baseline, it is possible that this episode and the 
one prior to admission were not due to TIAs. In both cases, she 
did not have any residual deficits.

Seizure was considered given her remote history of seizures due 
to benxo withdrawal per patient, but EEG this admission did not 
reveal notable abnormalities (including during the 4 am 
inpatient episode of word-finding difficulty). Given multiple 
stroke risk factors, history of paroxysmal a-fib, prior aortic 
valve replacement, and low INR on admission, TIA with a 
cardioembolic source is certainly on the differential.

During this admission, the patient was started on heparin gtt 
and bridged to therapeutic INR (1.5 -> 1.8 -> 2.1 on the day of 
discharge). Her BP was allowed to auto-regulate with goal 
SBP<180, as below. Stroke risk factors were assessed while 
in-house - HbA1c 6.0, lipds (chol 183, Triglyc 76, HDL 59, LDL 
109), TSH 0.68. TTE showed no evidence of PFO or intracardiac 
clot.

EXAMINATION:  MRI AND MRA BRAIN AND MRA NECK PT11 MR ___

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with word finding difficulty ? stroke  //

TECHNIQUE:  Three dimensional time of flight MR arteriography was performed
through the brain with maximum intensity projection reconstructions.

Dynamic MRA of the neck was performed during administration of 20 mL of
Multihance intravenous contrast.

Brain imaging was performed with sagittal T1 and axial FLAIR, T2, gradient
echo and diffusion technique.

Three dimensional maximum intensity projection and segmented images were
generated. This report is based on interpretation of all of these images. The
examination was performed using a 1.5T MRI.

COMPARISON:  CTA head and neck from ___

FINDINGS: 

The study is mildly degraded by motion limiting the evaluation.  Within this
confines:

MRI Brain:
There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, masses, mass effect, midline shift
or infarction.   The ventricles and sulci are patent and prominent in keeping
with age-related volume loss.

There are scattered foci and more confluent areas of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity
in the subcortical and periventricular white matter, nonspecific, likely
secondary to small vessel ischemic disease.

The orbits are unremarkable noting prior bilateral cataract surgeries.  There
is mucosal thickening with mucous retention cysts in bilateral maxillary
sinuses.  Also seen is mucosal thickening in bilateral ethmoid air cells.  The
remaining visualized paranasal sinuses are clear.  Nonspecific fluid
opacification of bilateral mastoid tip air cells.

MRA brain:  The right vertebral artery is not visualized on the unenhanced 3D
time-of-flight MRA of the brain.  However, on the postcontrast MRA of the neck
the right vertebral artery appears markedly hypoplastic with termination in
posterior inferior cerebellar artery.  The absence of visualization on the
head MRA is probably because of small size.

The intracranial vertebral and internal carotid arteries and their major
branches appear unremarkable without evidence of stenosis, occlusion, or
aneurysm formation.

There hypoplastic A1 segment of right anterior cerebral artery.

MRA neck:  There is 2 vessel aortic arch with common origin for the left
carotid artery and right brachiocephalic trunk.

The evaluation for the origin of right common carotid artery and right
vertebral artery is limited given the loss of signal on the MRA of the neck. 
The remaining common, internal and external carotid arteries appear normal. 
There is no evidence of internal carotid artery stenosis by NASCET criteria. 
The origins of the great vessels, subclavian and vertebral arteries appear
unremarkable bilaterally.

IMPRESSION:


1. No acute intracranial abnormality.
2. Absence of visualization of the right vertebral artery on 3D time-of-flight
MRA of the brain.  The contrast-enhanced neck MRA demonstrates markedly
diminutive right vertebral artery which probably terminates in ___. 
Otherwise, unremarkable MRA of the brain.
3. Evaluation for the origin of right common carotid and right vertebral
artery is limited given the loss of signal.  Otherwise, unremarkable MRA of
the neck.
